html:
The Pinikura, also spelt Binigura, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Pilbara region of Western Australia, around the lower Ashburton River. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours included the Kurrama to the north and the Jiwarli and Thiin to the south and east. Though they speak different languages, the Pinikura and the Puutu Kunti Kurrama now act together through one corporation for their lands.

Their country is iron ore country. In 2020 the mining company Rio Tinto blew up two rock shelters at Juukan Gorge that showed people had lived there for over 40,000 years. The destruction, legal under the law of the time, caused an outcry and the company's chief executive resigned.
